result.question:
There's an open corrective work order on Transformer 1 at site MAIN for the gassing problem, and the crew says the unit has settled down. I want to check that before we close it.

Find the open corrective work order on Transformer 1 that relates to gassing, discharge, overheating or oil treatment. Give me its number, description, priority, failure code and assigned technician. If there's more than one, work with the oldest and list the rest.

Then build two separate findings from the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000:
1. Screen hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model. List any flagged timestamps with their values.
2. Run a dissolved gas fault classification on the first and the last complete sample, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Tell me whether the class stayed the same, moved to a lower-energy or lower-temperature fault, or got worse.

Decide as follows:
- Close the work order only if both findings say it's calm: nothing is flagged in the last two samples, and the last class is the same as or milder than the first. Put both findings in the resolution notes and keep the existing failure code.
- If exactly one finding points to trouble, don't close it. Add a note saying which check disagreed, and recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days.
- If both findings point to trouble, keep it open and raise its priority by one level, but not above 1.

Count a sample as complete only if all five gases are non-null. If any of the three screened gases has fewer than 4 non-null samples, skip the model for that gas and flag any sample more than 50% above the gas's window mean as a manual outlier. If there's no matching open work order at all, say so, report both findings, and don't create anything.
result.answer:
No further tool calls are needed — no file pointer exists for the window and no materialize tool is exposed, so I'm applying the manual fallback screen and computing the DGA ratios directly.

## Work order search

**No matching open corrective work order was found on Transformer 1 at MAIN.** The only open WO is:

| WO | Description | Type | Status | Priority | Failure code | Technician |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | **PdM** (not CM) | APPR | 1 | none | none assigned |

Its long description mentions a confirmatory DGA oil sample, but it is a preventive/predictive OLTC inspection, not a corrective order for the gassing problem, and its scope (tap-changer contact inspection) would not be satisfied by calm gas readings. Per your rule I have **not closed, edited, or created anything**. If you consider 1000051 the WO you meant, tell me and I'll apply the decision logic below to it.

## Finding 1 – Anomaly screen (H₂, C₂H₄, C₂H₂), 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-18 (4 complete samples)

The TSFM anomaly detector could not be executed: the catalog has no anomaly-detection card, and no dataset file pointer for this window exists (prior result files don't record their input path; no materialize tool is available). I therefore applied your manual rule (>50 % above window mean) to all three gases:

| Gas | Samples (ppm) | Window mean | Flag threshold | Flagged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2845, 2950, 2800, 2900 | 2873.8 | 4310.6 | none |
| Ethylene | 16684, 16500, 16700, 16600 | 16621.0 | 24931.5 | none |
| Acetylene | 7, 6, 8, 7 | 7.0 | 10.5 | none |

**Nothing flagged**, including the last two samples (01-17, 01-18). Note the gases are stable but at very high absolute levels (TDCG-relevant, ethylene ~16,600 ppm).

## Finding 2 – DGA fault classification (IEC 60599 / Rogers ratios)

The `interpret_dga` LLM service was unavailable (3 attempts each), so ratios were computed directly:

| Sample | C₂H₂/C₂H₄ | CH₄/H₂ | C₂H₄/C₂H₆ | IEC 60599 class | Rogers code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 (first) | 0.0004 | 2.60 | 3.05 | **T2 – thermal fault 300–700 °C** | 0-2-2 (thermal >700 °C) |
| 2024-01-18 (last) | 0.0004 | 2.53 | 3.05 | **T2 – thermal fault 300–700 °C** | 0-2-2 (thermal >700 °C) |

**Class stayed the same** – no movement to a lower- or higher-energy fault. No arcing signature (acetylene negligible).

## Net assessment

Both findings say "calm" (stable, no outliers, unchanged class) — so under your rules a matching corrective WO would have been closable. However, (a) there is no matching corrective WO, and (b) Finding 1 is a manual fallback, not a model result, and the unchanged class is still an active high-temperature thermal fault at very high gas concentrations. I'd recommend keeping 1000051 open, completing the OLTC inspection, and taking the confirmatory lab DGA it already calls for before treating the gassing issue as resolved.

details.suggestions: The agent correctly queried open work orders for Transformer 1 at MAIN, retrieved the five gases over the exact window, identified all four samples as complete, and produced arithmetically correct manual outlier screens (means 2873.75 / 16621 / 7 ppm, nothing flagged) and correct IEC 60599 / Rogers ratio classifications (T2 both samples, class unchanged). It appropriately treated the only open WO (1000051, worktype PdM, OLTC inspection) as not a matching corrective order and, per the rules, created/closed/updated nothing while still reporting both findings and offering to apply the decision logic if the user considers 1000051 the intended WO. Gaps: it skipped iot.stream_extent and tsfm.data_quality, and although find_models returned no anomaly-detection card, it did not attempt tsfm.run_recipe before falling back to the manual >50% rule even though the fallback condition (fewer than 4 samples) was not met; the fallback was, however, clearly disclosed. The fmsr.interpret_dga failures ('LLM unavailable') were handled transparently with a manual ratio computation rather than fabricated output. Improvements: call stream_extent/data_quality first, attempt run_recipe with an explicit model or report its specific failure, and be more explicit that classifying 1000051 as non-matching is a judgment call given its long description references DGA gassing.
